name: JA Solar JAM66S30 510W (Large)
notes: Technology: PERC cells, 132 half-cell, monofacial with single 3.2mm glass - electrically it shares JA Solar's Deepblue 3.0 Pro platform, but JA Solar doesn't market it under that series name, so it has no documented `panel-series` and is tracked individually rather than grouped with a series-wide note. Pros: the highest-wattage 132-cell PERC module in this file. Cons: PERC lags TOPCon/HJT on temperature coefficient and degradation, and as an unnamed one-off it has less certainty around long-term availability than a named series.

name: JA Solar Deepblue 3.0 420W
notes: Technology: PERC cells, monofacial with single 3.2mm glass, split between a compact 108-cell format (420W) and a larger 132-cell format (500-505W). Pros: budget-friendly and ubiquitous, so it's easy to source and price-competitive against newer technology. Cons: PERC's weaker temperature coefficient and higher degradation than TOPCon/HJT rivals; the 132-cell bins are almost 2.1m long, so verify rafter spans, and note they are GSE Portrait Only.

name: JA Solar Deepblue 3.0 Pro 430W
notes: Technology: a mixed-technology series under one name - the 430-435W LR bins are PERC, monofacial with single glass, while the 435W MB bin swaps in N-Type TOPCon bifacial double-glass at the same headline wattage. Pros: the MB bin gets a materially better temperature coefficient and durability than the LR bins for no extra watts. Cons: the LR bins have a comparatively low Voc (verify cold-climate string counts), and buyers must check the model suffix (LR vs MB), not just the watt rating, since two very different panels share this series name.

name: JA Solar Deepblue 4.0 Pro 440W
notes: Technology: N-Type TOPCon cells, bifacial with dual glass, in the standard 108-cell format (440-465W, 1.6mm+1.6mm glass) plus a 600W large-format 144-cell variant (2.0mm+2.0mm glass) for commercial and utility roofs. Pros: bifacial TOPCon gives a strong temperature coefficient, low LID, and rear-side gain across the whole range. Cons: the 460W, 465W and 600W bins step up to a 30A series fuse versus 25A for the 440-450W bins, and the 600W variant is sized for utility-scale rather than residential arrays, so it isn't a drop-in swap for the smaller bins.

name: JA Solar DeepBlue 5.0 515W
notes: Technology: Bycium+ 5.0 N-Type TOPCon cells across two formats - the 162-cell (6x27) JAM54D51 line is monofacial with dual 2.0mm+2.0mm glass, while the 198-cell JAM66D50 line is genuinely bifacial with the same dual-glass build. Runs 515-670W across the two formats, succeeding DeepBlue 4.0 Pro as JA Solar's current flagship platform. Pros: JA Solar's highest efficiency to date (up to 24.8%) from a full-screen, gapless cell layout that boosts active silicon area, plus glass-glass durability on both formats. Cons: the large-format JAM66D50 is sized for commercial/utility roofs rather than standard residential arrays, and as JA Solar's newest platform, UK trade stock and pricing are less established than the long-running DeepBlue 4.0 Pro range.
